function: End-to-end learned CSI acquisition for beamforming: joint pilot and RIS phase-shift design with channel estimation (PPNet), then pilot compression, feedback and active/passive beamforming (RIS-E2ENet) (pp. 1-2, 7).
system: FDD downlink; BS ULA with 16 antennas, passive phase-only reflecting RIS 8x8 UPA, single-antenna UE, blocked direct link, 2.655 GHz band n7 (pp. 2, 3, 8).
method: CNN-based networks with multi-resolution blocks, pilots and RIS phases as trainable layers; PPNet trained with MSE loss to the true channel, RIS-E2ENet to maximize spectral efficiency (Eq. 26) (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa generating 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi LoS BS-RIS and RIS-UE channels at 2.655 GHz; 20,000 cascaded-channel samples, split 8:1:1 for training, validation and test (p. 8).
test_conditions: Same QuaDRiGa UMi-LoS site for training and testing (held-out 10%); sweeps over pilot power, pilot length, compression ratio, UE area size; no test on an unseen scenario reported (pp. 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned: random and DFT [20] pilot/phase shifts (PPNet). Learned: JDCNet [42] joint estimation-feedback, and Separate NN estimation, feedback, beamforming (RIS-E2ENet); ablated variants and upper bound (pp. 9-10).
metrics: NMSE of the cascaded channel, received pilot SNR, spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), FLOPs and parameter counts (pp. 8-12).
complexity: FLOPs formulas: PPNet about 9.57 million FLOPs at 32 pilots; RIS-E2ENet, Separate and online variant FLOPs and parameter counts, 95.70-99.99% UE-side reduction (pp. 9, 11-12).
q1_support: p. 8: "We use QuaDRiGa to generate the BS-RIS and RIS-UE CSI samples [39]. The Urban Micro (UMi) line-of-sight (LoS) scenario, as specified in 3GPP TR 38.901 [40], is employed"
q2_support: p. 8: "the dataset is split into training, validation, and test sets in an 8:1:1 ratio"; no model trained on one scenario or area is tested on another, and the UE-area sweep (Fig. 7, p. 10) states no train/test mismatch.
q3_support: p. 9: "PPNet significantly outperforms both random pilot and phase shift designs" (NMSE, Fig. 5); p. 10: "When compared to JDCNet [42], which jointly designs only the channel estimation and feedback modules, RIS-E2ENet achieves a performance improvement of 18.96%"
q4_support: p. 9: "For a pilot length of 32, the total FLOPs are approximately 9.57 million"; pp. 11-12 give the FLOPs and parameter counts of RIS-E2ENet, Separate and the online variant.
q5_support: p. 8: "A total of 20,000 different cascaded channel samples are generated" by the authors with QuaDRiGa; the 13 pages contain no code or data link or availability statement, and no public dataset is used.
notes: Title and DOI on page 1 match. Area 3 by the main-metric rule: the headline result is spectral efficiency (abstract, p. 1) and RIS-E2ENet outputs the precoder and RIS phase shifts (p. 7); the PPNet part (Sec. III, NMSE, pp. 5-6, 9) is channel estimation, so area 2 is the alternative for the reviewer. q3: the non-learned comparison (random, DFT) is on PPNet and the learned comparison (JDCNet, Separate) is on RIS-E2ENet; no non-learned baseline is run for RIS-E2ENet itself, since the DFT-equivalent pilot variants use the same networks (p. 10, Fig. 8). The online training-friendly variant is compared only over pilot power (Fig. 11, p. 11), not in a new scenario, hence q2 is 0.
